newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK businessman declares bid for post-97 leadership.
newsitem.headline: HK businessman declares bid for post-97 leadership.

text.p: A prominent Hong Kong businessman declared on Monday he would run for the territory's leadership after Britain hands back the colony to China in 1997.

Peter Woo, former chairman of Wharf (Holdings) Ltd and a member of the China-appointed body working on political arrangements for the transition, said he was entering the race to give the public more choice.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, reverts to China on July 1, 1997, as a Special Administration Region.

"I hereby solemnly declare my intention to seek nomination to the candidacy for the post of Chief Executive of the Special Administrative Region government in 1997," said Woo, son-in-law of the late shipping tycoon Sir Yue-kong Pao.
Woo is the fifth person to publicly put himself up as a successor to Britain's departing colonial governor Chris Patten.
Popularity polls put Patten's deputy Anson Chan far ahead of the five, although she has not stepped into the contest.
Former Chief Justic Sir Ti Liang Yang ranks second in the popularity stakes ahead of lawyer Lo Tak-shing.
Shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa, widely tipped as Beijing's favourite, is also in the running.
